description: Our team consists of 3 people from same high school but different fields. Our purpose is to be advanced engineers and make some new projects for our country and also The World.
summary: We are three high school students studying software and electrical-electronics engineering. Because we were curious about how fire behaves in space, we joined this NASA hackathon to gain real experience and inspire other students. Our mission is to make space fire research easier to understand through an interactive platform. The panel summarizes NASA’s free-fall rocket flame experiments, compares different rocket fuels, and runs fire simulations under various gravity and atmospheric conditions. We also included all the scientific sources we used. Finally, our built-in AI assistant, Alev AI, answers questions and guides users through the project.
details: Our project, “Flame in Free Fall,” is an interactive web application that helps users explore how fire may behave under different gravity, fuel, airflow, and cabin atmosphere conditions. It combines findings from NASA research with a simplified, clearly labeled model to compare scenarios and display predictions with uncertainty ranges. We built it using Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, and Plotly, and included an AI assistant to help explain the research and model results. Our goal is to make space fire research easier to understand and inspire students to explore science and technology. The creative part of our project is bringing research, interactive simulations, visual comparisons, and an AI guide together in one accessible platform. While developing it, we considered scientific sources, model limitations, uncertainty, and the importance of distinguishing predictions from real experimental measurements.
